title: A warmed liquid or gas expands, becomes less dense, and rises
summary: In physics a fluid is a liquid or a gas, and heating it makes it expand, become less dense, and rise.
body: OpenStax Physics says that in everyday speech fluid usually means a drink, but in physics a fluid is a liquid or a gas. As the temperature of a fluid increases, it expands and becomes less dense. The page calls the tendency to rise buoyancy, and it says convection is driven by that buoyancy: hot air rises because it is less dense than the surrounding air. In a pot, hotter water expands, decreases in density, and rises, while colder water sinks. The page does not give a density number for the air or the pot. Floating ice is a different card, from the Survey.
